title: Universal Input Controller Sync
problemStatement: Implement `createInputController({ value, defaultValue, onChange })` that correctly determines if an input is controlled (`value !== undefined`), manages an internal fallback state when uncontrolled, and synchronizes changes without triggering warnings.
interviewTrap: If an input starts with value={undefined} and later receives a string, React logs: 'A component is changing an uncontrolled input to be controlled'. Setting defaultValue or an empty string fallback prevents this.

testCases.name: Manages internal state when uncontrolled
testCases.testFn: const ctrl = createInputController({ defaultValue: '' }); ctrl.setValue('Hello'); return ctrl.getValue();

testCases.name: Defers to prop value when controlled

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: A controlled component's single source of truth is React state; an uncontrolled component delegates state to the DOM node via a ref. Bridging both requires synchronizing internal fallback state with incoming prop state.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is the difference between a Controlled component and an Uncontrolled component in React?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: In a Controlled component, the form element's value is driven by React state (`value={state}`, `onChange={e => setState(e.target.value)}`), making React the single source of truth. In an Uncontrolled component, the value is managed internally by the browser DOM itself, and React accesses values on demand via a `ref` (`ref.current.value`). Controlled components allow instant validation and formatting; uncontrolled components offer superior performance for high-frequency input.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Why does React warn 'A component is changing an uncontrolled input to be controlled'?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: This warning occurs when an input's initial value is `undefined` (making it uncontrolled by default) and later updates to a defined string value. React warns because switching modes mid-lifecycle causes state synchronization bugs. Fix it by always initializing state with an empty string `''` rather than `undefined` or `null`.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests understanding of controlled component lifecycle invariants.

realWorldUseCases.scenario: Universal Input Fields in UI Libraries
realWorldUseCases.description: Building text inputs that support being used as either controlled (`value` + `onChange`) or uncontrolled (`defaultValue`).
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: const isControlled = props.value !== undefined; const value = isControlled ? props.value : internalState;

howToExplain.opening: Controlled components treat React state as the single source of truth, while uncontrolled components delegate state to the browser DOM.
keyPoints: Never switch between controlled and uncontrolled mid-lifecycle.
Always default controlled input states to '' instead of undefined.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Understanding the controlled/uncontrolled boundary is critical for designing robust form architectures and design system inputs.
analogies: A puppet on strings (controlled) vs a wind-up toy (uncontrolled): the puppet moves only when you pull the strings; the wind-up toy moves on its own and you just check where it stopped.

commonMistakes.mistake: Passing value={data.name} where data.name is initially undefined.
commonMistakes.why: Causes React to mount the input as uncontrolled, and warn when data loads.

followUpDeepDive.question: How does React synchronize the real DOM input selection/cursor position in controlled inputs?
followUpDeepDive.answer: In `ReactDOMInput.js`, React records `selectionStart` and `selectionEnd` before updating the DOM node value and restores the cursor position immediately after to prevent the cursor jumping to the end on every keystroke.
